title: Court Case Preparation — August 10, 2026
description: Complete study module for your 74th District Court hearing

sections.title: Your Case Overview
sections.content: Case: 74th District Court, Bay City. Case Number: 26-4144-SC. Date: Monday, August 10, 2026, 9:30 AM. Magistrate: Perry. Incident: June 7, 2026 vehicle collision. Plaintiff: Jolene D. Wilcox. Amount claimed: $5,664.68 (vehicle damage, towing, storage). Key fact: The claim seeks only vehicle damage, towing, and storage — it does NOT include medical damages. However, the plaintiff's ER records (chest-wall contusion) ARE in the packet. Do NOT imply she has no medical evidence.

sections.title: Michigan Law Fundamentals
sections.content: Small claims jurisdiction: MCL 600.8401. Jurisdictional ceiling: $7,000 since January 1, 2024 (MCL 600.8401(e)). Statute of limitations: 3 years for tort claims (MCL 600.5805(2)). Burden of proof: plaintiff must prove damages by preponderance of evidence. Mini-tort (MCL 500.3135): capped at $3,000 for vehicle damage claims after July 1, 2020, to the extent not covered by insurance. This is an AMOUNT DEFENSE (reduces exposure), NOT a dismissal. Important: if the plaintiff's vehicle lacked no-fault insurance, mini-tort may be barred entirely (MCL 500.3135(4)(e)).

sections.title: Your Rights as Defendant
sections.content: Right to present evidence (bring all documents, photos, witnesses). Right to cross-examine witnesses (within informal hearing format). Right to request adjournment (NOT guaranteed — judge decides). NO ATTORNEY MAY APPEAR in small claims (MCL 600.8408(1)) — if you want a lawyer, case must be removed to general civil division before trial. Right to file counterclaim (must have independent legal basis and provable damages). Right to appeal magistrate decision to district judge within 7 days.

sections.title: What to Say
sections.content: SAFE: 'I'm here to respond to the claim.' 'I'd like to see proof of service.' 'The claim seeks only vehicle damage, towing, and storage — it does not include medical damages.' 'I'd like more time to prepare.' 'I have documentation of my own damages.'

sections.title: What NOT to Say
sections.content: DO NOT: Admit fault (the police report shows your vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign). Rely on the '$3,000 means I can't be sued' theory — this is WRONG. The $3,000 is a mini-tort cap on recovery, NOT a jurisdictional ceiling. Make emotional statements. Discuss legal theories you can't support. Say anything about insurance without careful thought.

sections.title: Court Procedure
sections.content: IMPORTANT: Both in-person AND Zoom are checked on your packet. Call the court (989-895-4232 or 989-895-4203) to CONFIRM before Monday. If in-person: arrive by 9:00 AM, check in with clerk, wait for case to be called. If Zoom: Meeting ID 946-661-3202, do NOT join early or late. Stand when speaking (if in-person). Address magistrate as 'Your Honor' or 'Magistrate Perry'. Present your response clearly. TAKE NOTES — there is NO court reporter and NO verbatim record (MCL 600.8411(2)). Your notes are the only record of what happened.

sections.title: Risk Assessment
sections.content: CRITICAL: The police report (UD-10, Officer Jacob Kirsch) states Unit 1 (your vehicle) failed to stop at the stop sign and caused the collision. This is documented evidence. The claim amount ($5,664.68) exceeds the mini-tort cap ($3,000). A finding against you on the mini-tort limits your exposure to $3,000 for vehicle damage. The claim also includes towing and storage which may be separately recoverable. Be prepared to respond to the stop-sign evidence without admitting fault.

quiz.question: What is the exact amount claimed by the plaintiff?
quiz.explanation: The exact amount is $5,664.68 (item 8 on the DC 84 form). This includes vehicle damage, towing, and storage.

quiz.question: What is the KEY fact about the claim?
options: The claim seeks only vehicle damage — no medical damages are pleaded
quiz.explanation: The claim seeks only vehicle damage, towing, and storage. No medical damages are in the claim. However, the plaintiff's ER records ARE in the packet — do not imply she has no medical evidence.

quiz.question: What should you say when you arrive?
options: 'I'm here to respond to the claim'
quiz.explanation: Start with 'I'm here to respond to the claim.' Be calm and professional.

quiz.question: What is Michigan's statute of limitations for tort claims?
quiz.explanation: Michigan has a 3-year statute of limitations for tort claims (MCL 600.5805(2)). Your incident was June 7, 2026 — well within the limit.

quiz.question: What is the current small claims jurisdictional ceiling in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: The ceiling is $7,000 since January 1, 2024 (MCL 600.8401(e)). Previously $6,500 (2021-2023).

quiz.question: Can an attorney represent you in Michigan small claims court?
options: Only if the judge allows it
No — attorneys are barred from small claims (MCL 600.8408(1))
quiz.explanation: Attorneys are generally barred from appearing in small claims (MCL 600.8408(1)). If you want a lawyer, the case must be removed to general civil division before trial.

quiz.question: What time should you arrive at the courthouse?
quiz.explanation: Arrive at 9:00 AM — 30 minutes early to find parking, go through security, and locate the courtroom. But FIRST confirm whether the hearing is in-person or Zoom by calling the court.

quiz.question: Should you admit fault if asked?
quiz.explanation: NEVER admit fault. The police report documents your vehicle failed to stop at a stop sign. Any admission compounds the comparative-fault position.

quiz.question: Is there a court reporter recording the hearing?
options: No — there is no verbatim record (MCL 600.8411(2))
quiz.explanation: There is NO court reporter and NO verbatim record in Michigan small claims (MCL 600.8411(2)). Your own notes are the only record. Take detailed notes.

quiz.question: What is the mini-tort cap for vehicle damage in Michigan?
quiz.explanation: The mini-tort cap is $3,000 for accidents after July 1, 2020 (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)). This is an amount defense that reduces recovery, NOT a jurisdictional ceiling that prevents the lawsuit.

quiz.question: What is the case number?
quiz.explanation: The case number is 26-4144-SC in the 74th District Court, Bay City. 'SC' stands for small claims.

quiz.question: Who is the plaintiff?
quiz.explanation: Jolene D. Wilcox is the plaintiff. Magistrate Perry presides over the hearing, and Officer Jacob Kirsch wrote the police report (UD-10).

quiz.question: What does the police report say about your vehicle?
options: It failed to stop at a stop sign
quiz.explanation: The UD-10 report (Officer Jacob Kirsch) states Unit 1 — your vehicle — failed to stop at the stop sign and caused the collision. This is documented evidence, so be prepared to respond without admitting fault.

quiz.question: What is the mini-tort cap for accidents after July 1, 2020?
quiz.explanation: The mini-tort cap is $3,000 for accidents after July 1, 2020 (MCL 500.3135(3)(e)). It limits recovery for vehicle damage to the extent not covered by insurance — an amount defense that reduces exposure, NOT a dismissal.

quiz.question: Can you file a counterclaim in small claims?
options: Yes, but it must have an independent legal basis and provable damages
No — counterclaims are not allowed in small claims
quiz.explanation: You may file a counterclaim (MCL 600.8405) if it has an independent legal basis and provable damages. It should be filed with your written response, before trial.

quiz.question: What happens if there's no court reporter?
options: A transcript is ordered from the court
Your notes are the only record of what happened
The magistrate's spoken summary is the official record
quiz.explanation: There is no court reporter and no verbatim record in Michigan small claims (MCL 600.8411(2)). Take detailed notes — they are the only record of what happened at the hearing.

quiz.question: The claim includes medical damages.
quiz.explanation: False. The claim seeks only vehicle damage, towing, and storage — no medical damages are pleaded. However, the plaintiff's ER records ARE in the packet — do not imply she has no medical evidence.

quiz.question: You can request a district judge instead of a magistrate.
quiz.explanation: True. Either party may demand removal of a small claims case to the general civil division (MCL 600.8405), where a district judge hears it instead of the magistrate. Note that removal also lifts the no-attorney restriction.

quiz.question: The statute of limitations has expired.
quiz.explanation: False. The incident was June 7, 2026 — about two months before the hearing. Michigan's tort statute of limitations is 3 years (MCL 600.5805(2)), so the claim is well within the limit.

quiz.question: Attorneys are barred from Michigan small claims court.
quiz.explanation: True. No attorney may appear in small claims (MCL 600.8408(1)). If you want a lawyer, the case must be removed to the general civil division before trial.
